candidate.title: RC-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle RC-Seq (retrotransposon capture sequencing) row of the supplied Illumina poster crop: bulk genomic DNA fractionation, solid-support microarray capture, paired-end sequencing and reference alignment. The card title and matching collection-page heading identify this target. CPT-Seq above, TN-Seq/INSeq below and the cytosine structures at right are adjacent context with no route into RC-Seq. The collection page mentions single-cell RC-seq, but that unshown adaptation is outside this assigned schematic. The cited Baillie et al. 2011 array-based implementation clarifies target termini and diagnostic genomic-flank linkage; this is not a claim that all RC-Seq implementations use arrays.

operations.label: Fractionate
operations.description: Convert long genomic DNA into shorter DNA fragments. Some fragments retain a retrotransposon target sequence together with neighboring genomic DNA.
operations.information_effect: Physical linkage between a retrotransposon sequence and its local genomic flank can remain on an individual fragment.

operations.label: Hybridize
operations.description: Hybridize the fractionated genomic DNA to complementary capture sites on a microarray, producing an array-associated, target-enriched DNA population. The array is the capture substrate, not a second biological sample.
operations.mechanism: Sequence-complementary hybridization to custom capture probes directed to retrotransposon termini.
operations.information_effect: Selectively enriches fragments near the targeted retrotransposon ends while retaining their genomic flanks. Enrichment does not imply perfect specificity or exhaustive detection of every insertion.

operations.label: Read1 / Read2 (paired-end sequencing; arrow unlabeled)
operations.description: Read the captured genomic DNA library by paired-end sequencing, shown as two opposing reads and a Sequenced fragment. The poster compresses the transition out of the array into an unlabeled arrow. The primary Figure 1b identifies release from the capture support by elution before Illumina sequencing; this is retained within the broad sequencing interface. Library construction is not decomposed into unshown operations.
operations.information_effect: Read pairs provide evidence linking retrotransposon sequence and a genomic locus. The readout carrier is genomic DNA enriched by capture, not RNA or newly synthesized probe products.

operations.label: Align
operations.description: Compare captured-fragment sequence data with the reference sequence and annotated transposon sites. The primary paper interprets read ends mapping together at one reference locus as a known insertion, and a pair with one end at a genomic locus and the other at a distal retrotransposon as evidence of a novel insertion. The two depicted outputs are alternative interpretation classes from one analysis, not separate library-preparation branches.
operations.information_effect: A diagnostic fragment can locate a retrotransposon-genome junction and identify a non-reference insertion. Establishing germline versus somatic status requires additional comparisons beyond this depicted reference alignment.
